recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If archival STU3/DSTU2 published pages still expose old broken links, that is outside the current FHIR source build and should be handled as an archival publication/site-maintenance task rather than by changing current source.
issue_request: FHIR-17217 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request raised against STU3. It reported that generated "Compare to DSTU2" footer links were malformed because the W3C htmldiff doc2 parameter inserted an extra F before the page name, for example Fexpansionprofile.html.
initial_application: No current Git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-17217. The historical symptom was in generated footer/link machinery rather than a resource-specific source file. A tightly related earlier Published issue, FHIR-12664, records the same broken Compare to DSTU2/W3C-link family and says it was handled in the build script/SVN history; later Git history moved and revised the compare-link footer implementation.
additional_context: The current build uses tools/templates/newfooter.html as the shared footer template, with many source and template pages including newfooter. Current compare links target R4, R5, and the last ballot through https://www.fhir.org/perl/htmldiff.pl using oldfile/newfile parameters and the normal <%rellink%> / <%baseURL%><%rellink%> values. Current source and active templates contain no Compare to DSTU2 text, W3C htmldiff doc1/doc2 parameters, or doc2 URL with the extra-F pattern reported by the Jira. Later compare-link commits also replaced stale W3C diff references.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current build no longer contains the broken DSTU2/doc2 compare-link construction and the active footer compare links do not insert an extra character before the page name.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published report of a broken Compare to DSTU2 W3C htmldiff link; its Jira comments say the issue came from build-script generation and was overridden in SVN history, supporting that FHIR-17217 belonged to historical link-generation machinery rather than current resource content.
